title: Do optimal policies really seek power? A gridworld audit of the Turner et al. power-seeking theorem

original_idea.body:
# Gridworld Audit of the Power-Seeking Theorem

Reproduce theorem via value iteration, then violate assumptions (heavy-tailed rewards, sub-optimal policies, discount sweeps).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: maps where the power-seeking guarantee weakens, sharpening instrumental-convergence threat models.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Small gridworlds, value iteration; CPU, accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused reproduction-plus-assumption-violation; breadth from multiple violation axes.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Neglected long-horizon instrumental-convergence problem, CPU-only, zero lab dependency.

low_compute.reasoning: Value iteration on toy MDPs, CPU.

novelty.reasoning: Power-seeking has gridworld follow-ups; the systematic assumption-violation sweep may be partially open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Gridworld follow-ups exist; systematic assumption-violation may be open.
